decisions.choice: an oracle: a solemn message from God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "lift up", and is used for a message the prophet lifts up his voice to deliver. Older translations rendered it "burden". It heads Zechariah 9:1 and 12:1 in the same way: "An oracle: the word of the LORD". |

decisions.choice: Malachi: the prophet's name, which means "my messenger"
alternatives: "my messenger", as a title rather than a name
decisions.reason: The name means "my messenger", the same word the LORD uses in 3:1 ("I am sending my messenger"). Nothing else is known of the prophet, and some think the word here is a title drawn from 3:1, not a personal name. The Greek translation is generally said to read "by the hand of his messenger", and the Aramaic Targum adds "whose name is called Ezra the scribe". The book is read here as the words of a prophet named Malachi.

decisions.choice: the time of Malachi: after the temple was rebuilt, in the Persian period
decisions.reason: The temple is standing and sacrifices are offered (1:10; 3:1, 10), and a governor rules (1:8), so the book comes from after 515 BC. Its concerns, careless priests, marriage to foreign wives, and tithes withheld, are those Ezra and Nehemiah dealt with in the middle of the fifth century BC (Ezra 9-10; Nehemiah 13), so it is usually dated near their time. |

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD to Israel: a series of disputes
decisions.reason: The book is built of six disputes (1:2-5; 1:6-2:9; 2:10-16; 2:17-3:5; 3:6-12; 3:13-21), each following one pattern: the LORD makes a statement, the people object, "But you say, ...?", and the LORD answers. "Israel" here is the whole people of God living in Judah after the exile. |

decisions.choice: oracle (L, B), message (R); the disputes set in lines
decisions.reason: Massa' follows the Isaiah table. Malachi is close to prose, but it is a prophet's oracle and its verses divide clearly at the Hebrew accents, so it is set in lines at every level, breaking at the main accent and, where a verse is long, at the lesser ones. The people's questions are set in double quotes and the LORD's words have none, as in Isaiah. |

decisions.choice: I have loved you: the LORD's covenant love, by which he chose his people
decisions.reason: The love meant here is the LORD's choice of Israel and his faithfulness to that choice. "It was not because you were more numerous than any other people that the LORD set his love on you ... but because the LORD loved you" (Deuteronomy 7:7-8). The book begins with this love before any rebuke. |

decisions.choice: But you say, "How have you loved us?": the pattern of the disputes
decisions.reason: The people answer every statement of the LORD with a question that challenges it (1:6, 7; 2:14, 17; 3:7, 8, 13). Here they doubt that he loves them at all, after years of hardship. The questions are quoted words of the people. |

decisions.choice: Esau and Jacob: the ancestors of Edom and Israel
decisions.reason: Esau and Jacob were twin sons of Isaac; Esau's descendants became the people of Edom, south-east of Judah, and Jacob's became Israel (Genesis 25:23-30; 36:1). Though they were brothers, the LORD chose Jacob, the younger. |

decisions.choice: And I loved Jacob (L), Even so, I loved Jacob (B); Yet I chose to love Jacob (R)
decisions.reason: With the first words of verse 3, the line reads "I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated" (L, B) and "I chose to love Jacob, but I rejected Esau" (R), the wording published in Romans 9:13. The LORD's question "How have you loved us?" uses the deity_pronoun setting, because the people speak to him. |

decisions.choice: the people's objection: "Pero ustedes dicen: «¿En qué ...?»" (L), "Y aun así ustedes preguntan: «¿De qué manera ...?»" (B), "Pero ustedes preguntan: «¿Cómo ...?»" (R), with plural_you spans
decisions.reason: Malachi repeats this objection through the book (1:6, 7; 2:14, 17; 3:7, 8, 13); each level keeps one wording so the pattern of the disputes shows. The LORD speaks to the people and the priests as a group, so every "you" takes the plural_you span (ustedes / vosotros), verbs included.

decisions.choice: I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated: I chose Jacob, and did not choose Esau
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, "love" and "hate" set side by side often mean preferring one and setting the other aside, not the feelings the words usually name. Jacob "loved" Rachel and "hated" Leah, meaning he loved her less (Genesis 29:30-31); Deuteronomy 21:15 speaks of a loved wife and a "hated" one. Jesus' saying that his followers must "hate" their families (Luke 14:26) is given in Matthew 10:37 as loving them "more than me". Here the LORD chose Jacob to be his people and did not choose Esau.

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 9:13
decisions.reason: Paul quotes "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated" in Romans 9:13 to show that God's choice rests on his own purpose, not on what people do. |

decisions.choice: his mountains a desolation: the ruin of Edom
decisions.reason: Edom's land was the hill country of Seir, south-east of the Dead Sea. After the fall of Jerusalem, Edom itself was overrun, by the Babylonian king Nabonidus in the 550s BC and then by Arab peoples moving in from the desert, who later became the Nabateans. By Malachi's day its towns lay in ruins. |

decisions.choice: but I rejected Esau (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "Esau I hated", and Readable says "I rejected Esau", as in Romans 9:13 at each level. The idiom decision (m1) explains the sense. |

source.text: כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֨ר אֱד֜וֹם רֻשַּׁ֗שְׁנוּ וְנָשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנֶ֣ה חֳרָב֔וֹת כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הֵ֥מָּה יִבְנ֖וּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶהֱר֑וֹס וְקָרְא֤וּ לָהֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל רִשְׁעָ֔ה וְהָעָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־זָעַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Though Edom says, We have been shattered, but we will return and build [the] ruins, thus says Yahweh of hosts: They will build, but I will tear down; and they will be called [the] territory of wickedness, and the people with whom Yahweh is indignant forever.

en.L: If Edom says, "We have been shattered, but we will return and build the ruins," \q thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: They will build, but I will tear down; \q and they will be called the territory of wickedness, \q and the people with whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is indignant forever.
en.B: Edom may say, "We have been crushed, but we will rebuild the ruins." \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: They may build, but I will tear down. \q They will be called the Land of Wickedness, \q the people with whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is angry forever.
en.R: The people of Edom may say, "Our towns have been destroyed, but we will build them again." \q But this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: They can build, but I will tear it all down. \q People will call their country the Land of Evil, \q and they will be known as the people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is always angry with.

es.L: Si Edom dice: «Hemos sido destrozados, pero volveremos y edificaremos las ruinas», \q así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: Ellos edificarán, pero yo derribaré; \q y los llamarán territorio de maldad \q y pueblo contra el cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está indignado para siempre.
es.B: Edom podrá decir: «Hemos sido aplastados, pero reconstruiremos las ruinas». \q Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: Ellos podrán edificar, pero yo derribaré. \q Los llamarán Tierra de Maldad, \q el pueblo contra el cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está airado para siempre.
es.R: La gente de Edom podrá decir: «Nuestras ciudades han sido destruidas, pero las volveremos a construir». \q Pero esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Ellos podrán construir, pero yo lo derribaré todo. \q La gente llamará a su país Tierra de Maldad, \q y todos sabrán que son el pueblo con el que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está siempre enojado.

fr.L: Si Édom dit : « Nous sommes écrasés, mais nous reviendrons et nous bâtirons les ruines », \q ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Eux bâtiront, mais moi, je démolirai ; \q et on les appellera territoire de méchanceté \q et peuple contre qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est irrité pour toujours.
fr.B: Édom peut dire : « Nous avons été écrasés, mais nous rebâtirons les ruines. » \q Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Qu’ils bâtissent, moi je démolirai. \q On les appellera Pays de la Méchanceté, \q le peuple contre qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est irrité pour toujours.
fr.R: Les Édomites peuvent dire : « Nos villes ont été détruites, mais nous allons les reconstruire. » \q Mais voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Ils peuvent construire, moi, je démolirai tout. \q On appellera leur pays le Pays du Mal, \q et on les connaîtra comme le peuple contre qui {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est toujours en colère.

sw.L: Ijapokuwa Edomu husema, "Tumepondwa, lakini tutarudi na kujenga magofu," \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Wao watajenga, lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitabomoa; \q nao wataitwa nchi ya uovu, \q na watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewaghadhibikia milele.
sw.B: Edomu yaweza kusema, "Tumevunjwa, lakini tutajenga upya magofu." \q Lakini hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Wao wanaweza kujenga, lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitabomoa. \q Wataitwa Nchi ya Uovu, \q watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewakasirikia milele.
sw.R: Watu wa Edomu wanaweza kusema, "Miji yetu imeharibiwa, lakini tutaijenga tena." \q Lakini hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Wanaweza kujenga, lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitabomoa kila kitu. \q Watu wataiita nchi yao Nchi ya Uovu, \q nao watajulikana kuwa watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huwakasirikia daima.

vi.L: Nếu Ê-đôm nói: "Chúng ta đã bị đập tan, nhưng chúng ta sẽ trở lại và xây dựng những nơi đổ nát," \q thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Chúng sẽ xây, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phá đổ; \q người ta sẽ gọi chúng là lãnh thổ của sự gian ác, \q và là dân mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi giận đời đời.
vi.B: Ê-đôm có thể nói: "Chúng ta đã bị đập nát, nhưng chúng ta sẽ xây lại những nơi đổ nát." \q Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Chúng cứ xây, còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phá đổ. \q Chúng sẽ bị gọi là Xứ Gian Ác, \q là dân mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giận đến đời đời.
vi.R: Dân Ê-đôm có thể nói: "Các thành của chúng ta đã bị phá hủy, nhưng chúng ta sẽ xây lại." \q Nhưng đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Chúng có thể xây, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phá đổ tất cả. \q Người ta sẽ gọi xứ của chúng là Xứ Gian Ác, \q và ai cũng biết chúng là dân mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giận mãi mãi.

ko.L: 에돔이 "우리가 부서졌으나 돌아가서 폐허를 세우겠다" 하고 말하여도, \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 그들은 세우겠지만 나는 허물겠다. \q 사람들이 그들을 악의 영토라 부르고, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 영원히 분노하는 백성이라 부를 것이다.
ko.B: 에돔은 "우리가 무너졌지만 폐허를 다시 쌓겠다" 하고 말할지 모른다. \q 그러나 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 그들이 쌓아도 나는 허물어 버리겠다. \q 사람들은 그들을 '악한 땅'이라 부르고, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 영원히 노여워하는 백성이라 할 것이다.
ko.R: 에돔 사람들은 "우리 성읍들이 무너졌지만 다시 세우겠다" 하고 말할지 모른다. \q 그러나 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 그들이 세워도 나는 다 허물어 버리겠다. \q 사람들은 그들의 나라를 '악한 나라'라고 부르고, \q 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 언제나 노여워하는 백성으로 알려질 것이다.

decisions.choice: Edom's words: a boast that it will recover
decisions.reason: Edom's own words are quoted. It admits the ruin but expects to rebuild. The LORD answers that he will undo whatever it builds. |

decisions.choice: the territory of wickedness: a name that shows what they are
decisions.reason: Israel's land is called the LORD's holy land (Zechariah 2:16); Edom's will be named for its wickedness. "The people with whom the LORD is indignant" is a second such name. |

decisions.choice: indignant forever: under the LORD's lasting anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to be indignant, to denounce or curse (Numbers 23:7-8; Proverbs 24:24). Edom's fall is lasting, unlike Israel's, which the LORD reversed. |

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L), The LORD of Armies says this (B), This is what the LORD of Armies says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the Isaiah table. Edom's words are quoted in double quotes. Balanced and Readable write "Land of Wickedness" and "Land of Evil" with capitals as a name. |

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR de los ejércitos" (L), "el SEÑOR de los Ejércitos" (B, R); "Así dice ..." / "... dice esto" / "Esto es lo que dice ..."; at the end of a sentence "dice el SEÑOR de los ejércitos / Ejércitos"
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet for the LORD of hosts and "Thus says". Malachi uses the title more than twenty times, mostly in "says the LORD of hosts", which keeps the plain "dice" at every level.

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR des armées" at every level; "Ainsi parle ..." / "... dit ceci" / "Voici ce que dit ..."; at the end of a sentence "dit le SEIGNEUR des armées"
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet. The English says "of Armies" at B and R; French keeps « des armées », its published wording at every level.

decisions.choice: "BWANA wa majeshi" at every level; "BWANA wa majeshi asema hivi" / "Hivi ndivyo ... asemavyo" / "Hili ndilo ... analosema"; at the end of a sentence "asema BWANA wa majeshi" (L, B), "anasema BWANA wa majeshi" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet, never "Sabaoth".

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân" at every level, the span on CHÚA only; "says the LORD of hosts" is "CHÚA Vạn Quân phán" at every level; "Thus says" is "phán thế này" / "phán như vầy" / "Đây là lời ... phán"
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet, which keeps "phán vậy" for ne'um and the plain "phán" for 'amar.

decisions.choice: 만군의 주 (L, B), 하늘의 군대를 거느린 주 (R, in God's own mouth; 거느리신 in "Thus says"); "says the LORD of hosts" is 만군의 주가 말한다 (L, B) / 하늘의 군대를 거느린 주가 말한다 (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet. "Thus says" keeps 께서 even in God's mouth, as Isaiah settled; the closing formula is God naming himself, without -시-.

source.text: וְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם תִּרְאֶ֑ינָה וְאַתֶּ֤ם תֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל לִגְב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And your eyes will see, and you will say, Great [is] Yahweh beyond the border of Israel.

en.L: Your own eyes will see it, \q and you will say, "Great is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q beyond the border of Israel!"
en.B: You will see it with your own eyes, \q and you will say, "Great is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q even beyond the borders of Israel!"
en.R: You will see this for yourselves. \q Then you will say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great, \q even outside the land of Israel!"

es.L: Y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos [lo] verán, \q y {{plural_you:ustedes dirán|vosotros diréis}}: «¡Grande es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} \q más allá de la frontera de Israel!»
es.B: Lo {{plural_you:verán ustedes|veréis vosotros}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios ojos, \q y {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: «¡Grande es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q aun más allá de las fronteras de Israel!»
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} mismos lo {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}. \q Entonces {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es grande, \q aun fuera de la tierra de Israel!»

fr.L: Vos yeux le verront, \q et vous direz : « Grand est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} \q au-delà de la frontière d’Israël ! »
fr.B: Vous le verrez de vos propres yeux, \q et vous direz : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est grand, \q même au-delà des frontières d’Israël ! »
fr.R: Vous le verrez vous-mêmes. \q Alors vous direz : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est grand, \q même en dehors du pays d’Israël ! »

sw.L: Na macho yenu yataona, \q nanyi mtasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mkuu \q kupita mpaka wa Israeli!"
sw.B: Mtaona kwa macho yenu wenyewe, \q nanyi mtasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mkuu, \q hata nje ya mipaka ya Israeli!"
sw.R: Mtajionea wenyewe. \q Ndipo mtasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mkuu, \q hata nje ya nchi ya Israeli!"

vi.L: Mắt các ngươi sẽ thấy, \q và các ngươi sẽ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật vĩ đại \q vượt ra ngoài bờ cõi Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.B: Chính mắt các ngươi sẽ thấy điều đó, \q và các ngươi sẽ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật vĩ đại, \q ngay cả bên ngoài bờ cõi Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.R: Các ngươi sẽ tự mình thấy điều ấy. \q Khi ấy các ngươi sẽ nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật vĩ đại, \q ngay cả bên ngoài đất Y-sơ-ra-ên!"

ko.L: 너희 눈이 [그것을] 볼 것이고, \q 너희는 이렇게 말할 것이다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 위대하시다, \q 이스라엘 국경 너머에서도!"
ko.B: 너희가 너희 눈으로 직접 보고, \q 이렇게 말할 것이다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 위대하시다. \q 이스라엘 국경 밖에서도!"
ko.R: 너희는 이 일을 직접 보게 될 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 이렇게 말할 것이다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 위대하시다. \q 이스라엘 땅 밖에서도 그러하시다!"

decisions.choice: beyond the border of Israel: the LORD's greatness reaches past Israel's land
decisions.reason: The words can mean "above" or "beyond" the border. Most take them as "beyond": the LORD's rule is seen in what he does to Edom, outside Israel. Read the other way, the people praise him for what he does over Israel's own land.

decisions.choice: you will say: the doubters of verse 2 will praise
decisions.reason: Those who asked "How have you loved us?" will answer their own question when they see what happens to Edom. |

decisions.choice: the people's words in double quotes
decisions.reason: The people's words of praise are quoted, as their questions are. |

decisions.choice: the people's praise uses -시- for God (주께서는 위대하시다)
decisions.reason: People speaking about God give him the honorific, as the terms sheet; only God's own words about himself leave it out.

source.text: בֵּ֛ן יְכַבֵּ֥ד אָ֖ב וְעֶ֣בֶד אֲדֹנָ֑יו וְאִם־אָ֣ב אָ֣נִי אַיֵּ֣ה כְבוֹדִ֡י וְאִם־אֲדוֹנִ֣ים אָנִי֩ אַיֵּ֨ה מוֹרָאִ֜י אָמַ֣ר׀יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת לָכֶם֙ הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ בּוֹזֵ֣י שְׁמִ֔י וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם בַּמֶּ֥ה בָזִ֖ינוּ אֶת־שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: A son honors [his] father, and a slave his master. And if I [am] a father, where [is] my honor? And if I [am] a master, where [is] my fear? says Yahweh of hosts to you, the priests, despisers of my name. And you say, In what have we despised your name?

en.L: A son honors [his] father, and a slave his master. \q And if a father [am] I, where [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} honor? And if a master [am] I, where [is] the fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts to you, O priests, who despise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. \q But you say, "How have we despised {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name?"
en.B: A son honors his father, and a servant honors his master. \q If I am a father, where is the honor due to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? If I am a master, where is the respect due to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies to you priests who despise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. \q Yet you ask, "In what way have we despised {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name?"
en.R: A son honors his father, and a servant respects his master. \q I am a father to you, so why do you not honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? I am your master, so why do you not respect {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. You priests treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name with contempt! \q But you ask, "How have we treated {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name with contempt?"

es.L: El hijo honra al padre, y el esclavo a su señor. \q Pues si yo [soy] padre, ¿dónde [está] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} honra? Y si yo [soy] señor, ¿dónde [está] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} temor?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, oh sacerdotes, que {{plural_you:desprecian|despreciáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: «¿En qué hemos despreciado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre?»
es.B: El hijo honra a su padre, y el siervo honra a su señor. \q Si yo soy padre, ¿dónde está la honra que se {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} debe? Si soy señor, ¿dónde está el respeto que se {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} debe?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sacerdotes que {{plural_you:desprecian|despreciáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q Y aun así {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿De qué manera hemos despreciado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre?»
es.R: Un hijo honra a su padre, y un siervo respeta a su amo. \q Yo soy un padre para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; entonces, ¿por qué no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:honran|honráis}}? Soy {{plural_you:su señor|vuestro señor}}; ¿por qué no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:respetan|respetáis}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. ¡{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, sacerdotes, {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre con desprecio! \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿Cómo hemos tratado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre con desprecio?»

fr.L: Un fils honore [son] père, et un esclave son maître. \q Et si je suis père, où est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} honneur ? Et si je suis maître, où est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} crainte ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, à vous, ô prêtres, qui méprisez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. \q Mais vous dites : « En quoi avons-nous méprisé {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ? »
fr.B: Un fils honore son père, et un serviteur honore son maître. \q Si je suis père, où est l’honneur qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est dû ? Si je suis maître, où est le respect qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est dû ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, à vous, prêtres, qui méprisez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. \q Et vous demandez : « En quoi avons-nous méprisé {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ? »
fr.R: Un fils honore son père, et un serviteur respecte son maître. \q Je suis un père pour vous : pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honorez-vous pas ? Je suis votre maître : pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} respectez-vous pas ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. Vous, les prêtres, vous traitez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom avec mépris ! \q Mais vous demandez : « Comment avons-nous traité {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom avec mépris ? »

sw.L: Mwana humheshimu baba [yake], na mtumwa bwana wake. \q Basi ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni baba, heshima {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iko wapi? Na ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni bwana, kicho {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} kiko wapi? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi kwenu, enyi makuhani mnaolidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Nanyi mwasema, "Tumelidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kwa namna gani?"
sw.B: Mwana humheshimu baba yake, na mtumishi humheshimu bwana wake. \q Ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni baba, iko wapi heshima ninayostahili? Ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni bwana, iko wapi staha ninayostahili? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi kwenu ninyi makuhani mnaolidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumelidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kwa namna gani?"
sw.R: Mwana humheshimu baba yake, na mtumishi humstahi bwana wake. \q Mimi ni baba yenu, basi kwa nini hamniheshimu? Mimi ni bwana wenu, basi kwa nini hamnistahi? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. Ninyi makuhani mnalidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}! \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumelidharau jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kwa jinsi gani?"

vi.L: Con trai tôn kính cha, và đầy tớ [tôn kính] chủ mình. \q Vậy nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cha, sự tôn kính dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là chủ, sự kính sợ dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán với các ngươi, hỡi các thầy tế lễ khinh dể danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Nhưng các ngươi nói: "Chúng tôi đã khinh dể danh Chúa ở chỗ nào?"
vi.B: Con trai tôn kính cha mình, và đầy tớ tôn kính chủ mình. \q Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cha, thì sự tôn kính dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là chủ, thì lòng kính sợ dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán với các ngươi, là những thầy tế lễ khinh dể danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã khinh dể danh Chúa bằng cách nào?"
vi.R: Con trai tôn kính cha mình, và đầy tớ kính trọng chủ mình. \q Ta là cha của các ngươi, vậy sao các ngươi không tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? Ta là chủ của các ngươi, vậy sao các ngươi không kính trọng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. Hỡi các thầy tế lễ, các ngươi coi thường danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã coi thường danh Chúa bằng cách nào?"

ko.L: 아들은 [그] 아버지를 공경하고, 종은 그의 주인을 [공경한다]. \q 그런데 내가 아버지라면 나에 대한 공경은 어디 있느냐? 내가 주인이라면 나에 대한 두려움은 어디 있느냐? 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 내 이름을 멸시하는 제사장들아, 너희에게 말한다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 무엇으로 주님의 이름을 멸시했습니까?" 하고 말한다.
ko.B: 아들은 아버지를 공경하고, 종은 주인을 공경한다. \q 내가 아버지라면 나에게 돌아올 공경은 어디 있느냐? 내가 주인이라면 나에게 돌아올 존경은 어디 있느냐? 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 내 이름을 멸시하는 너희 제사장들에게 말한다. \q 그런데도 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님의 이름을 멸시했습니까?" 하고 묻는다.
ko.R: 아들은 아버지를 공경하고, 종은 주인을 존경한다. \q 나는 너희의 아버지인데, 어찌하여 너희는 나를 공경하지 않느냐? 나는 너희의 주인인데, 어찌하여 너희는 나를 존경하지 않느냐? 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 너희 제사장들은 내 이름을 업신여긴다! \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님의 이름을 업신여겼습니까?" 하고 묻는다.

decisions.choice: a slave and his master: a servant owned by his master
decisions.reason: The word means a servant who belonged to his master, not a hired worker. Such a servant owed his master obedience and respect, as a son owed honor to his father. The LORD is both father (2:10; Isaiah 63:16) and master to his people. |

decisions.choice: where is my fear: where is the respect owed to me
decisions.reason: "Fear" here is reverence and respect, the honor a servant owes his master. |

decisions.choice: who despise my name: who treat the LORD himself with contempt
decisions.reason: The LORD's name stands for the LORD himself, as he has made himself known (Exodus 3:15). The priests, whose task was to honor it, show contempt for it by what they offer (verses 7-8). |

decisions.choice: the priests: the dispute of 1:6-2:9 is addressed to the priests
decisions.reason: The priests served at the altar of the rebuilt temple. The LORD's charge against them runs to 2:9, where it ends with his covenant with Levi. |

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word follows the style guide's rule: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable, with the servant's position stated in m1. The people's question is set in double quotes and uses the deity_pronoun setting, because they speak to the LORD. |

decisions.choice: "esclavo" (L), "siervo" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave", as the English L; Balanced and Readable say "siervo", the published word for a servant who belongs to his master.

decisions.choice: "esclave" (L), "serviteur" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave", as the English L.

decisions.choice: "mtumwa" (L), "mtumishi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave", as the English L; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word for a servant.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ" at every level
decisions.reason: The servant here stands for God's people before their master, so the rule that God's servants are "đầy tớ" at every level holds; the meaning decision says he belonged to his master.

decisions.choice: 종 at every level; "fear" as 두려움 (L), 존경 (B, R)
decisions.reason: 종 is the settled word for a servant at every level, and the English L's "slave" is carried by the meaning decision. "My fear" is the respect owed to the master, as m2.

source.text: מַגִּישִׁ֤ים עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִי֙ לֶ֣חֶם מְגֹאָ֔ל וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמֶּ֣ה גֵֽאַלְנ֑וּךָ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֕ם שֻׁלְחַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה נִבְזֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: [You are] presenting on my altar defiled food. And you say, In what have we defiled you? In your saying, [The] table of Yahweh, it [is] despicable.

en.L: You are presenting defiled food on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. \q But you say, "How have we defiled {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?" \q By your saying, \q "The table of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is despicable."
en.B: You offer defiled food on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. \q Yet you ask, "In what way have we defiled {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?" \q By saying, \q "The table of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may be despised."
en.R: You put food on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar that is not fit to offer. \q But you ask, "How have we made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} unclean?" \q You do it by saying, "We do not need to respect {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar."

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes presentan|Vosotros presentáis}} sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar alimento contaminado. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: «¿En qué {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos contaminado?» \q En que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: \q «La mesa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} es despreciable».
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes ofrecen|Vosotros ofrecéis}} alimento contaminado sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar. \q Y aun así {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿De qué manera {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos contaminado?» \q Al decir: \q «La mesa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} puede ser despreciada».
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes ponen|Vosotros ponéis}} sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar alimentos que no son dignos de ofrecerse. \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes preguntan|vosotros preguntáis}}: «¿Cómo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} hemos hecho impuro?» \q Lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} cuando {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «No hace falta respetar el altar {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Vous présentez sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel une nourriture souillée. \q Mais vous dites : « En quoi {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons-nous souillé ? » \q En disant : \q « La table {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est méprisable. »
fr.B: Vous offrez sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel une nourriture souillée. \q Et vous demandez : « En quoi {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons-nous souillé ? » \q En disant : \q « La table {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, on peut la mépriser. »
fr.R: Vous mettez sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel des aliments indignes d’être offerts. \q Mais vous demandez : « Comment {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons-nous rendu impur ? » \q Vous le faites en disant : « Pas besoin de respecter l’autel {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Mnaleta juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} chakula kilichotiwa unajisi. \q Nanyi mwasema, "Tumekutia unajisi kwa namna gani?" \q Kwa kusema kwenu, \q "Meza ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni ya kudharauliwa."
sw.B: Mnatoa chakula kilichotiwa unajisi juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumekutia unajisi kwa namna gani?" \q Kwa kusema, \q "Meza ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yaweza kudharauliwa."
sw.R: Mnaweka juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} chakula kisichofaa kutolewa. \q Lakini mnauliza, "Tumekutia unajisi kwa jinsi gani?" \q Mnafanya hivyo mnaposema, "Hatuna haja ya kuiheshimu madhabahu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

vi.L: Các ngươi dâng trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thức ăn ô uế. \q Nhưng các ngươi nói: "Chúng tôi đã làm ô uế Chúa ở chỗ nào?" \q Ấy là khi các ngươi nói: \q "Bàn của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thật đáng khinh."
vi.B: Các ngươi dâng thức ăn ô uế trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã làm ô uế Chúa bằng cách nào?" \q Ấy là khi các ngươi nói: \q "Bàn của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} có thể bị khinh thường."
vi.R: Các ngươi đặt trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} những thức ăn không xứng đáng để dâng. \q Thế mà các ngươi hỏi: "Chúng tôi đã làm ô uế Chúa bằng cách nào?" \q Các ngươi làm điều đó khi nói: "Chẳng cần tôn trọng bàn thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."

ko.L: 너희가 내 제단 위에 더러워진 음식을 바치고 있다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 무엇으로 주님을 더럽혔습니까?" 하고 말한다. \q 너희가 이렇게 말하는 것이다. \q "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 상은 멸시받을 만하다."
ko.B: 너희는 내 제단에 더러운 음식을 바친다. \q 그런데도 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님을 더럽혔습니까?" 하고 묻는다. \q 너희가 이렇게 말하기 때문이다. \q "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 상은 멸시해도 된다."
ko.R: 너희는 바칠 자격이 없는 음식을 내 제단에 올려놓는다. \q 그런데 너희는 "저희가 어떻게 주님을 더럽혔습니까?" 하고 묻는다. \q 너희는 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 제단은 존중하지 않아도 된다" 하고 말함으로써 그렇게 한다.

decisions.choice: defiled food: offerings unfit for the altar
decisions.reason: The sacrifices are called the "food" of God (Leviticus 21:6, 8; 3:11), not because he needs to eat but because they are presented at his table. Verse 8 says what makes them defiled. |

decisions.choice: the table of the LORD: the altar
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 41:22 and 44:16 call the altar "the table that is before the LORD". The priests treat the place where the LORD is served as of no account. |

decisions.choice: How have we defiled you?: defiling the offering defiles the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "defiled you": to treat his altar with contempt is to treat the LORD himself so. The Greek translation is generally said to read "defiled it", referring to the food.

decisions.choice: the people's words in double quotes
decisions.reason: The priests did not say these words aloud; their actions say them. They are set as quoted words, as the book quotes the people throughout. Readable says "altar" for "table", the sense of m2. |

source.text: וְכִֽי־תַגִּשׁ֨וּן עִוֵּ֤ר לִזְבֹּ֨חַ֙ אֵ֣ין רָ֔ע וְכִ֥י תַגִּ֛ישׁוּ פִּסֵּ֥חַ וְחֹלֶ֖ה אֵ֣ין רָ֑ע הַקְרִיבֵ֨הוּ נָ֜א לְפֶחָתֶ֗ךָ הֲיִּרְצְךָ֙א֚וֹ הֲיִשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֔יךָ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And when you present a blind [one] for sacrifice, [is it] not evil? And when you present [the] lame and [the] sick, [is it] not evil? Present it, please, to your governor; will he be pleased with you or lift up your face? says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And when you present a blind [animal] for sacrifice, is it not evil? \q And when you present the lame and the sick, is it not evil? \q Present it, please, to your governor; will he be pleased with you or lift up your face? \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: When you offer blind animals in sacrifice, is that not wrong? \q When you offer animals that are lame or sick, is that not wrong? \q Just try offering such a thing to your governor! Would he be pleased with you or receive you kindly? \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: You bring blind animals to sacrifice. Is that not wrong? \q You bring animals that are lame or sick. Is that not wrong? \q Try giving them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:presentan|presentáis}} un [animal] ciego para el sacrificio, ¿no es malo? \q Y cuando {{plural_you:presentan|presentáis}} el cojo y el enfermo, ¿no es malo? \q Preséntalo, pues, a tu gobernador; ¿se agradará de ti o te levantará el rostro?, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}} animales ciegos en sacrificio, ¿no está mal? \q Cuando {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}} animales cojos o enfermos, ¿no está mal? \q ¡Intenta ofrecerle algo así a tu gobernador! ¿Se agradaría de ti o te recibiría con favor?, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales ciegos para sacrificarlos. ¿No está mal eso? \q {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales cojos o enfermos. ¿No está mal eso? \q ¡{{plural_you:Intenten|Intentad}} regalárselos a {{plural_you:su gobernador|vuestro gobernador}}! ¿Se pondría contento con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}? ¿{{plural_you:Los|Os}} aceptaría?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Et quand vous présentez une [bête] aveugle pour le sacrifice, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Et quand vous présentez la boiteuse et la malade, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Présente-la donc à ton gouverneur : sera-t-il content de toi, ou relèvera-t-il ta face ? \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Quand vous offrez des bêtes aveugles en sacrifice, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Quand vous offrez des bêtes boiteuses ou malades, n’est-ce pas mal ? \q Essaie donc d’offrir cela à ton gouverneur ! Serait-il content de toi, t’accueillerait-il avec faveur ? \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Vous apportez des bêtes aveugles pour les sacrifier. N’est-ce pas mal ? \q Vous apportez des bêtes boiteuses ou malades. N’est-ce pas mal ? \q Essayez donc de les offrir à votre gouverneur ! Serait-il content de vous ? Vous accepterait-il ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Nanyi mnapomtoa [mnyama] kipofu kuwa dhabihu, je, si uovu? \q Na mnapomtoa aliye kilema na aliye mgonjwa, je, si uovu? \q Basi mpelekee liwali wako; je, atapendezwa nawe, au atauinua uso wako? \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Mnapotoa wanyama vipofu kuwa dhabihu, je, si vibaya? \q Mnapotoa wanyama vilema au wagonjwa, je, si vibaya? \q Hebu jaribu kumpa liwali wako kitu kama hicho! Je, angependezwa nawe au kukupokea kwa wema? \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Mnaleta wanyama vipofu kuwa dhabihu. Je, si vibaya? \q Mnaleta wanyama vilema au wagonjwa. Je, si vibaya? \q Jaribuni kumpa liwali wenu wanyama hao! Je, angefurahishwa nanyi? Je, angewapokea? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Khi các ngươi dâng [con vật] mù làm sinh tế, chẳng phải là điều ác sao? \q Khi các ngươi dâng con què và con bệnh, chẳng phải là điều ác sao? \q Hãy dâng nó cho quan tổng đốc của ngươi xem; người có hài lòng về ngươi hay nâng mặt ngươi lên không? \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Khi các ngươi dâng những con vật mù làm sinh tế, chẳng phải là sai sao? \q Khi các ngươi dâng những con vật què hay bệnh, chẳng phải là sai sao? \q Thử đem dâng thứ đó cho quan tổng đốc của ngươi xem! Người có hài lòng về ngươi hay tiếp đón ngươi tử tế không? \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: Các ngươi đem những con vật mù đến dâng làm sinh tế. Như thế chẳng phải là sai sao? \q Các ngươi đem những con vật què hay bệnh. Như thế chẳng phải là sai sao? \q Thử đem chúng biếu quan tổng đốc của các ngươi xem! Ông ấy có vui lòng với các ngươi không? Ông ấy có tiếp nhận các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

ko.L: 너희가 눈먼 [짐승]을 제물로 바칠 때, 그것이 악하지 않으냐? \q 다리 저는 것과 병든 것을 바칠 때, 그것이 악하지 않으냐? \q 그것을 너의 총독에게 바쳐 보아라. 그가 너를 기뻐하겠느냐, 너의 얼굴을 들어 주겠느냐? \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 너희가 눈먼 짐승을 제물로 바치니, 그것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 다리 절거나 병든 짐승을 바치니, 그것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 그런 것을 너의 총독에게 바쳐 보아라! 그가 너를 기뻐하거나 반갑게 맞아 주겠느냐? \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희는 눈먼 짐승을 제물로 가져온다. 그것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 다리 절거나 병든 짐승을 가져온다. 그것이 잘못이 아니냐? \q 그런 것을 너희 총독에게 선물로 바쳐 보아라! 그가 너희를 반기겠느냐? 너희를 받아 주겠느냐? 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: blind, lame and sick animals: animals the law forbade for sacrifice
decisions.reason: Animals for sacrifice had to be without defect: blind, lame or sick animals were not to be offered (Leviticus 22:20-25; Deuteronomy 15:21). The priests were letting people offer what they did not want themselves. |

decisions.choice: your governor: the Persian governor of Judah
decisions.reason: Judah was a province of the Persian empire, ruled by a governor, as Zerubbabel had been (Haggai 1:1) and Nehemiah later was (Nehemiah 5:14-15). People brought gifts to a governor, and no one would dare give him a sick animal. |

decisions.choice: lift up your face: receive you with favor
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to accept him, to grant his request (Genesis 32:21; Job 42:8). The same idiom returns in verse 9. |

decisions.choice: is it not evil?: a question
decisions.reason: The words can be read as the LORD's question or as the priests' careless claim ("It does not matter!"). Read either way, the LORD's verdict is plain.

decisions.choice: animals (B, R); wrong (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "[animal]"; Balanced and Readable say "animals". Balanced and Readable say "wrong" for "evil", which here means a wrong done. |

decisions.choice: "Preséntalo ... a tu gobernador" (L), "¡Intenta ofrecerle algo así a tu gobernador!" (B) in the singular; plural at R
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here, as if to each priest; Literal and Balanced follow it, Readable keeps the plural of the rest of the verse, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Présente-la donc à ton gouverneur" (L), "Essaie donc d'offrir cela à ton gouverneur" (B) in the singular; "vous" at R
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here; Literal and Balanced follow its number, Readable keeps "vous" with the rest of the verse.

decisions.choice: "mpelekee liwali wako" (L), "jaribu kumpa liwali wako" (B) in the singular; plural at R
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here; Literal and Balanced follow its number.

decisions.choice: "quan tổng đốc của ngươi" (L, B) in the singular; "của các ngươi" at R
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here; Literal and Balanced follow its number. "Tổng đốc" is the published word for the Persian governor (Ezra).

decisions.choice: 너의 총독 (L, B) in the singular; 너희 총독 at R
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here; Literal and Balanced follow its number.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֛ה חַלּוּ־נָ֥א פְנֵי־אֵ֖ל וִֽיחָנֵ֑נוּמִיֶּדְכֶם֙ הָ֣יְתָה זֹּ֔את הֲיִשָּׂ֤א מִכֶּם֙ פָּנִ֔ים אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, entreat, please, [the] face of God, that he may be gracious to us. From your hand this has been; will he lift up faces from you? says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And now, entreat the face of God, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may be gracious to us! \q From your hand this has come; \q will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lift up the face of any of you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: So now, plead with God to be gracious to us! \q With such offerings from your hands, \q will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} show favor to any of you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: So now, go ahead and ask God to be kind to us! \q But when you bring offerings like these, \q will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accept any of you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: ¡Y ahora, {{plural_you:imploren|implorad}} el rostro de Dios para que tenga piedad de nosotros! \q De {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}} ha venido esto; \q ¿levantará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} el rostro de alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Así que ahora, ¡{{plural_you:rueguen|rogad}} a Dios que tenga piedad de nosotros! \q Con semejantes ofrendas de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}, \q ¿mostrará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} favor a alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Así que ahora, ¡{{plural_you:vayan|id}} y {{plural_you:pídanle|pedidle}} a Dios que sea bondadoso con nosotros! \q Pero si {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} ofrendas como estas, \q ¿aceptará {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Et maintenant, implorez donc la face de Dieu, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce ! \q De votre main cela est venu ; \q relèvera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la face de l’un de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Alors maintenant, suppliez Dieu de nous faire grâce ! \q Avec de telles offrandes de vos mains, \q accordera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur à l’un de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Alors maintenant, allez-y, demandez à Dieu d’être bon envers nous ! \q Mais si vous apportez de telles offrandes, \q acceptera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’un de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Basi sasa, ombeni kibali mbele ya uso wa Mungu, ili atufanyie neema! \q Jambo hili limetoka mkononi mwenu; \q je, atamwinulia uso yeyote kati yenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Basi sasa, mwombeni Mungu atufanyie neema! \q Kwa sadaka kama hizi kutoka mikononi mwenu, \q je, atamkubali yeyote kati yenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Basi sasa, nendeni mkamwombe Mungu atuhurumie! \q Lakini mnapoleta sadaka kama hizi, \q je, atampokea yeyote kati yenu? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy nài xin trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban ơn cho chúng ta! \q Điều này đến từ tay các ngươi; \q liệu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có nâng mặt ai trong các ngươi lên chăng? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, hãy cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời ban ơn cho chúng ta! \q Với những lễ vật như thế từ tay các ngươi, \q liệu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có đoái đến ai trong các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ, cứ đi cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời thương xót chúng ta đi! \q Nhưng khi các ngươi đem dâng những lễ vật như thế, \q liệu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chấp nhận ai trong các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

ko.L: 이제 너희는 하나님의 얼굴에 간청하여, 그분께서 우리에게 은혜를 베푸시게 하여라! \q 이것이 너희 손에서 나왔으니, \q 그분께서 너희 가운데 누구의 얼굴을 들어 주시겠느냐? 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 그러니 이제 하나님께 우리에게 은혜를 베풀어 달라고 간구해 보아라! \q 너희 손으로 이런 제물을 바치면서, \q 그분께서 너희 가운데 누구를 받아 주시겠느냐? 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 그러니 이제 하나님께 우리를 너그럽게 대해 달라고 빌어 보아라! \q 그러나 너희가 이런 제물을 가져오면서, \q 그분께서 너희 가운데 누구를 받아 주시겠느냐? 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: entreat the favor of God: seek his goodwill in prayer
decisions.reason: The phrase means "soften the face" of someone, that is, to seek favor (Exodus 32:11; 1 Kings 13:6). |

decisions.choice: a call to prayer, spoken in irony
decisions.reason: The prophet urges the priests to pray for the people ("us"), but with offerings like theirs the LORD will not hear. The question at the end expects the answer "no". |

decisions.choice: from your hand this has come: this is your doing
decisions.reason: The defective offerings came from the priests' own hands, so the LORD's refusal is their own fault. |

decisions.choice: entreat the favor (L), plead with God (B), ask God to be kind (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the face (m1). Balanced and Readable add "with such offerings" and "offerings like these" to make "this" plain. |

decisions.choice: God in the third person takes -시- here (그분께서 … 베푸시게)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the call to prayer as the prophet's own ironic words to the priests ("us"), so the honorific follows the rule for people speaking about God.

source.text: מִ֤י גַם־בָּכֶם֙ וְיִסְגֹּ֣ר דְּלָתַ֔יִם וְלֹֽא־תָאִ֥ירוּ מִזְבְּחִ֖י חִנָּ֑ם אֵֽין־לִ֨י חֵ֜פֶץ בָּכֶ֗ם אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּמִנְחָ֖ה לֹֽא־אֶרְצֶ֥ה מִיֶּדְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who also among you [is there] that he would shut the doors, and you would not kindle my altar in vain? I have no pleasure in you, says Yahweh of hosts, and an offering I will not accept from your hand.

en.L: Who is there even among you who would shut the doors, \q so that you would not kindle {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar in vain? \q I have no pleasure in you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and an offering I will not accept from your hand.
en.B: If only one of you would close the temple doors \q and stop you from lighting useless fires on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar! \q I have no pleasure in you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q and I will not accept an offering from your hands.
en.R: I wish someone among you would lock the temple doors, \q so that you would stop lighting useless fires on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar! \q I am not pleased with you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q I will not accept any offering you bring.

es.L: ¿Quién hay también entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que cierre las puertas, \q para que no {{plural_you:enciendan|encendáis}} en vano {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar? \q No tengo complacencia en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q y no aceptaré ofrenda de {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}}.
es.B: ¡Ojalá alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cerrara las puertas del templo \q y {{plural_you:les|os}} impidiera encender fuegos inútiles en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar! \q No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} complazco en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q ni aceptaré ofrenda de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}.
es.R: ¡Cómo quisiera que alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cerrara con llave las puertas del templo, \q para que {{plural_you:dejaran|dejarais}} de encender fuegos inútiles en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} altar! \q No estoy contento con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. \q No aceptaré ninguna ofrenda que {{plural_you:traigan|traigáis}}.

fr.L: Qui donc parmi vous fermerait les portes, \q pour que vous n’allumiez pas en vain {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel ? \q Je ne prends pas plaisir en vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et je n’accepterai pas d’offrande de votre main.
fr.B: Si seulement l’un de vous fermait les portes du temple \q pour que vous cessiez d’allumer des feux inutiles sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel ! \q Je ne prends aucun plaisir en vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et je n’accepterai pas d’offrande de vos mains.
fr.R: J’aimerais que l’un de vous ferme à clé les portes du temple, \q pour que vous arrêtiez d’allumer des feux inutiles sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} autel ! \q Je ne suis pas content de vous, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. \q Je n’accepterai aucune offrande que vous apporterez.

sw.L: Ni nani pia kati yenu angefunga milango, \q ili msiwashe moto juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} bure? \q Sina furaha kwenu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q wala sitakubali sadaka kutoka mkononi mwenu.
sw.B: Laiti mmoja wenu angefunga milango ya hekalu \q mkaacha kuwasha moto usiofaa juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}! \q Sina furaha nanyi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q wala sitakubali sadaka kutoka mikononi mwenu.
sw.R: Natamani mtu mmoja kati yenu afunge milango ya hekalu, \q ili mwache kuwasha moto usio na faida juu ya madhabahu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}! \q Sipendezwi nanyi, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. \q Sitakubali sadaka yoyote mtakayoleta.

vi.L: Ai trong các ngươi sẽ đóng các cửa lại, \q để các ngươi khỏi nhóm lửa trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cách vô ích? \q Ta không vui lòng về các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không nhận lễ vật từ tay các ngươi.
vi.B: Ước gì có một người trong các ngươi đóng cửa đền thờ lại, \q để các ngươi thôi nhóm lửa vô ích trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Ta không hài lòng về các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không nhận lễ vật từ tay các ngươi.
vi.R: Ta ước gì có ai trong các ngươi khóa cửa đền thờ lại, \q để các ngươi thôi nhóm những ngọn lửa vô ích trên bàn thờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Ta không vui lòng về các ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Ta sẽ không nhận bất cứ lễ vật nào các ngươi đem đến.

ko.L: 너희 가운데 누가 문들을 닫아서, \q 너희가 내 제단에 헛되이 불을 피우지 못하게 하겠느냐? \q 나는 너희를 기뻐하지 않는다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 나는 너희 손에서 제물을 받지 않겠다.
ko.B: 너희 가운데 누가 성전 문을 닫아 \q 너희가 내 제단에 쓸데없이 불을 피우지 못하게 하면 좋겠다! \q 나는 너희를 기뻐하지 않는다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 나는 너희 손에서 바치는 제물을 받지 않겠다.
ko.R: 너희 가운데 누군가가 성전 문을 잠가 버려서, \q 너희가 내 제단에 쓸데없이 불을 피우지 못하게 되면 좋겠다! \q 나는 너희가 마음에 들지 않는다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희가 가져오는 제물은 어떤 것도 받지 않겠다.

decisions.choice: who among you would shut the doors?: a wish
decisions.reason: A question beginning "who" can express a wish (2 Samuel 15:4; Psalm 55:7). The LORD would rather have the temple closed than receive such worship. |

decisions.choice: the doors: the gates of the temple courts
decisions.reason: The doors are those of the temple and its courts, where the altar stood. Shutting them would end the sacrifices. |

decisions.choice: offering: a gift brought to God
decisions.reason: The word is used for the grain offering (Leviticus 2:1) and for offerings in general. Here it means any gift the priests bring. |

decisions.choice: the temple doors (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which doors are meant (m2). |

source.text: כִּ֣י מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֜מֶשׁ וְעַד־מְבוֹא֗וֹ גָּד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבְכָל־מָק֗וֹם מֻקְטָ֥ר מֻגָּ֛שׁ לִשְׁמִ֖י וּמִנְחָ֣ה טְהוֹרָ֑ה כִּֽי־גָד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: For from [the] rising of [the] sun and to its setting great [is] my name among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for great [is] my name among the nations, says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: For from the rising of the sun to its setting great [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name among the nations, \q and in every place incense is brought near to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and a pure offering; \q for great [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name among the nations, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: From where the sun rises to where it sets, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is great among the nations. \q In every place incense is offered to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and pure offerings, \q because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is great among the nations, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: From where the sun rises to where it sets, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is honored among the nations. \q Everywhere people burn incense to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and bring offerings that are pure. \q My name is great among the nations, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Porque desde la salida del sol hasta su ocaso, grande [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre entre las naciones, \q y en todo lugar se presenta incienso a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y una ofrenda pura; \q porque grande [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre entre las naciones, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Desde donde sale el sol hasta donde se oculta, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es grande entre las naciones. \q En todo lugar se quema incienso en honor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre y se presentan ofrendas puras, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es grande entre las naciones, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: De oriente a occidente, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es honrado entre las naciones. \q En todas partes la gente {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} quema incienso y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} trae ofrendas puras. \q Mi nombre es grande entre las naciones, \q dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Car du lever du soleil jusqu’à son coucher, grand [est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom parmi les nations, \q et en tout lieu on présente de l’encens à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, ainsi qu’une offrande pure ; \q car grand [est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom parmi les nations, \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Du soleil levant au soleil couchant, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est grand parmi les nations. \q En tout lieu, on fait monter l’encens vers {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et l’on apporte des offrandes pures, \q parce que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est grand parmi les nations, \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: De l’est à l’ouest, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est honoré parmi les nations. \q Partout, les gens {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} brûlent de l’encens et {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}apportent des offrandes pures. \q Mon nom est grand parmi les nations, \q dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Kwa maana tangu kuchomoza kwa jua hata kutua kwake jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} [ni] kuu kati ya mataifa, \q na kila mahali uvumba unaletwa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na sadaka safi; \q kwa maana jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} [ni] kuu kati ya mataifa, \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Tangu jua linapochomoza hadi linapotua, jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni kuu kati ya mataifa. \q Kila mahali uvumba unafukizwa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na sadaka safi zinatolewa, \q kwa sababu jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni kuu kati ya mataifa, \q asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Kutoka mashariki hadi magharibi, jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} linaheshimiwa kati ya mataifa. \q Kila mahali watu wananifukizia uvumba na kuniletea sadaka safi. \q Jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni kuu kati ya mataifa, \q anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Vì từ nơi mặt trời mọc cho đến nơi mặt trời lặn, danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lớn giữa các dân tộc, \q và tại mọi nơi người ta dâng hương cho danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, cùng một lễ vật tinh sạch; \q vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lớn giữa các dân tộc, \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Từ phương mặt trời mọc đến phương mặt trời lặn, danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lớn lao giữa các dân tộc. \q Khắp mọi nơi người ta xông hương và dâng lễ vật tinh sạch cho danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lớn lao giữa các dân tộc, \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: Từ đông sang tây, danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được tôn trọng giữa các dân tộc. \q Khắp nơi người ta đốt hương cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và dâng lên những lễ vật tinh sạch. \q Danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thật lớn lao giữa các dân tộc, \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

ko.L: 해 뜨는 곳에서부터 해 지는 곳까지 민족들 가운데서 내 이름이 크고, \q 곳곳마다 내 이름에 분향하며 깨끗한 제물을 바친다. \q 민족들 가운데서 내 이름이 크기 때문이다. \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 해가 뜨는 곳에서 해가 지는 곳까지, 민족들 가운데서 내 이름이 크다. \q 곳곳에서 사람들이 내 이름 앞에 향을 피우고 깨끗한 제물을 바친다. \q 내 이름이 민족들 가운데서 크기 때문이다. \q 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 동쪽에서 서쪽 끝까지, 민족들이 내 이름을 높인다. \q 어디서나 사람들이 나에게 향을 피우고 깨끗한 제물을 바친다. \q 내 이름은 민족들 가운데서 위대하다. \q 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun to its setting: from east to west, all over the world
decisions.reason: The phrase means the whole earth (Psalm 50:1; 113:3; Isaiah 45:6). |

decisions.choice: my name is great among the nations: the LORD honored by the nations, now or in time to come
alternatives: my name will be great among the nations
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb "is" or "will be", and the offering is described with participles, so the verse may speak of the present or of the future. Read as present, it may mean that the nations, in their own way, honor the God of heaven, or that Jews scattered among the nations worship him; read as future, it is a promise like Zephaniah 2:11 and Isaiah 45:6. Either way it shames the priests of verse 10. From early times Christian writers read it of the church's worship among the nations. The text leaves the time open, and the wording here keeps the Hebrew present.

decisions.choice: incense is offered: offerings burned, as the smoke of incense
decisions.reason: The first word means something made to go up in smoke, usually incense. The offerings brought "in every place" contrast with the defiled offerings in the one temple. |

decisions.choice: is honored (R); burn incense to me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "honored" for "great" in the first line and keeps "great" in the third, and says "burn incense to me" for "incense is offered to my name", since the name stands for the LORD himself. |

decisions.choice: "grande [es] mi nombre" with no tense (L); present "es grande" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb (meaning decision m2); Spanish follows the English in the present and leaves the future reading to that decision.

decisions.choice: "dâng hương" (L), "xông hương" (B), "đốt hương" (R)
decisions.reason: The offering of incense is said with the ordinary Vietnamese verbs at each level; "lễ vật tinh sạch" is the pure offering.

source.text: וְאַתֶּ֖ם מְחַלְּלִ֣ים אוֹת֑וֹ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֗ם שֻׁלְחַ֤ן אֲדֹנָי֙ מְגֹאָ֣ל ה֔וּא וְנִיב֖וֹ נִבְזֶ֥ה אָכְלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: But you [are] profaning it in your saying, [The] table of [the] Lord, it [is] defiled, and its fruit, its food, [is] despicable.

en.L: But you are profaning it \q in your saying, "The table of the Lord, it is defiled, \q and its fruit, its food, is despicable."
en.B: But you profane it \q by saying, "The Lord's table is defiled, \q and the food on it can be despised."
en.R: But you treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name as if it were not holy. \q You say, "The Lord's altar is unclean, \q and the food offered on it does not deserve respect."

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo {{plural_you:están profanando|estáis profanando}} \q al decir: «La mesa del Señor está contaminada, \q y su fruto, su alimento, es despreciable».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo {{plural_you:profanan|profanáis}} \q cuando {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «La mesa del Señor está contaminada, \q y su comida puede despreciarse».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre como si no fuera santo. \q {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}}: «El altar del Señor está impuro, \q y la comida que se ofrece en él no merece respeto».

fr.L: Mais vous, vous le profanez \q en disant : « La table du Seigneur est souillée, \q et son fruit, sa nourriture, est méprisable. »
fr.B: Mais vous le profanez \q en disant : « La table du Seigneur est souillée, \q et ce qu’on y sert peut être méprisé. »
fr.R: Mais vous traitez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom comme s’il n’était pas saint. \q Vous dites : « L’autel du Seigneur est impur, \q et la nourriture qu’on y offre ne mérite aucun respect. »

sw.L: Lakini ninyi mnalitia unajisi \q kwa kusema kwenu, "Meza ya Bwana imetiwa unajisi, \q na tunda lake, chakula chake, ni cha kudharauliwa."
sw.B: Lakini ninyi mnalitia unajisi \q kwa kusema, "Meza ya Bwana imetiwa unajisi, \q na chakula kilicho juu yake chaweza kudharauliwa."
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mnalitendea jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kana kwamba si takatifu. \q Mnasema, "Madhabahu ya Bwana ni najisi, \q na chakula kinachotolewa juu yake hakistahili heshima."

vi.L: Nhưng các ngươi đang làm ô uế danh ấy \q khi các ngươi nói: "Bàn của Chúa bị ô uế, \q và hoa lợi của nó, thức ăn của nó, thật đáng khinh."
vi.B: Nhưng các ngươi làm ô uế danh ấy \q khi nói: "Bàn của Chúa đã bị ô uế, \q và thức ăn trên đó có thể khinh thường."
vi.R: Nhưng các ngươi đối xử với danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như thể nó không thánh. \q Các ngươi nói: "Bàn thờ của Chúa không tinh sạch, \q và thức ăn dâng trên đó chẳng đáng được tôn trọng."

ko.L: 그러나 너희는 그것을 더럽히고 있다. \q 너희가 말하기를 "주님의 상, 그것은 더러워졌고, \q 그 열매, 곧 그 음식은 멸시받을 만하다" 하니 말이다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희는 내 이름을 더럽힌다. \q 너희가 "주님의 상은 더러워졌으니, \q 그 위의 음식은 업신여겨도 된다" 하고 말하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희는 내 이름을 거룩하지 않은 것처럼 대한다. \q 너희는 "주님의 제단은 깨끗하지 않고, \q 그 위에 바치는 음식은 존중할 가치가 없다" 하고 말한다.

decisions.choice: profaning it: profaning the LORD's name
decisions.reason: "It" is the name the nations honor (verse 11). To profane is to treat what is holy as common. |

decisions.choice: its fruit, its food: what is offered on the altar
decisions.reason: The first word, "its fruit", is rare and may mean the produce brought to the altar, or the priests' share of it. Some think it is a copying slip, written twice. "Its food" explains it.

decisions.choice: the table of the Lord is defiled: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: The charge of verse 7 is repeated. Here the word for the Lord is Adonai, not the divine name. |

decisions.choice: treat my name as if it were not holy (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "it" refers to and what profaning means (m1). |

decisions.choice: "el Señor" for Adonai, with no setting span
decisions.reason: Adonai is kept apart from the divine name, as the English keeps "the Lord" apart from "the LORD".

decisions.choice: "le Seigneur" for Adonai, with no setting span
decisions.reason: Adonai is kept apart from the divine name, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Bwana" for Adonai, with no setting span
decisions.reason: Adonai is kept apart from BWANA, as the English keeps "the Lord" apart from "the LORD".

decisions.choice: "Chúa" for Adonai, never in capitals and with no span
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet: Adonai is "Chúa", kept apart from CHÚA.

decisions.choice: 주님 for Adonai
decisions.reason: As the terms sheet: a bare 주 never stands for the divine name, and 주님 is Adonai.

source.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּם֩ הִנֵּ֨ה מַתְּלָאָ֜ה וְהִפַּחְתֶּ֣ם אוֹת֗וֹ אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וַהֲבֵאתֶ֣ם גָּז֗וּל וְאֶת־הַפִּסֵּ֨חַ֙ וְאֶת־הַ֣חוֹלֶ֔ה וַהֲבֵאתֶ֖ם אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֑ה הַאֶרְצֶ֥ה אוֹתָ֛הּ מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you say, Look, what a weariness! And you sniff at it, says Yahweh of hosts; and you bring [what was] stolen and the lame and the sick, and you bring the offering. Will I accept it from your hand? says Yahweh.

en.L: And you say, "Look, what a weariness!" and you sniff at it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; \q and you bring what was stolen, and the lame and the sick; \q and you bring the offering! \q Shall I accept it from your hand? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: You say, "What a burden this is!" and you sniff at it in contempt, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q You bring animals that were stolen, or lame or sick, \q and these you bring as your offering! \q Should I accept that from your hands? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You say, "We are so tired of all this!" And you turn up your noses at it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q You bring animals that were stolen, or lame, or sick, \q and you offer them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q Should I accept them from you? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «¡He aquí, qué fatiga!», y {{plural_you:resoplan|resopláis}} contra ello, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos; \q y {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} lo robado, y el cojo y el enfermo; \q ¡y {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} la ofrenda! \q ¿La aceptaré yo de {{plural_you:su mano|vuestra mano}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}}: «¡Qué carga es esta!», y lo {{plural_you:miran|miráis}} con desprecio, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. \q {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales robados, cojos o enfermos, \q ¡y eso es lo que {{plural_you:presentan|presentáis}} como ofrenda! \q ¿Habré de aceptarlo de {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Dicen|Decís}}: «¡Qué cansados estamos de todo esto!», y {{plural_you:arrugan|arrugáis}} la nariz con desprecio, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. \q {{plural_you:Traen|Traéis}} animales robados, o cojos, o enfermos, \q ¡y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} los {{plural_you:ofrecen|ofrecéis}}! \q ¿Debo aceptarlos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et vous dites : « Voici, quelle fatigue ! » et vous soufflez dessus, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées ; \q et vous apportez ce qui a été volé, et la [bête] boiteuse et la malade ; \q et vous apportez l’offrande ! \q L’accepterai-je de votre main ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Vous dites : « Quel fardeau ! » et vous soufflez dessus avec mépris, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. \q Vous amenez des bêtes volées, boiteuses ou malades, \q et c’est cela que vous apportez en offrande ! \q Devrais-je l’accepter de vos mains ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Vous dites : « Nous en avons assez de tout ça ! » Et vous faites la grimace, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées. \q Vous amenez des bêtes volées, boiteuses ou malades, \q et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} les offrez ! \q Devrais-je les accepter de vous ? dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nanyi mwasema, "Tazama, ni taabu iliyoje!" nanyi mnaibeua, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi; \q nanyi mnaleta kilichonyang'anywa, na kilicho kilema na kilicho mgonjwa; \q nanyi mnaleta sadaka! \q Je, nitaikubali kutoka mkononi mwenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mnasema, "Huu ni mzigo ulioje!" na mnaibeua kwa dharau, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. \q Mnaleta wanyama walionyang'anywa, vilema au wagonjwa, \q na hao ndio mnaowaleta kuwa sadaka yenu! \q Je, niikubali hiyo kutoka mikononi mwenu? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mnasema, "Tumechoka na mambo haya yote!" Nanyi mnayadharau, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. \q Mnaleta wanyama walionyang'anywa, au vilema, au wagonjwa, \q na mnanitolea hao! \q Je, niwakubali kutoka kwenu? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Các ngươi nói: "Kìa, thật là mệt nhọc!" và các ngươi khịt mũi khinh dể nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán; \q các ngươi đem đến con vật bị cướp, con què và con bệnh; \q và các ngươi đem đến lễ vật! \q Ta có nên nhận nó từ tay các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.
vi.B: Các ngươi nói: "Thật là gánh nặng!" rồi khịt mũi khinh thường, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Các ngươi đem đến những con vật bị cướp, què hoặc bệnh, \q và đó là những gì các ngươi đem dâng làm lễ vật! \q Ta có nên nhận lễ vật ấy từ tay các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.
vi.R: Các ngươi nói: "Chúng ta chán ngấy những việc này rồi!" Và các ngươi bĩu môi khinh khỉnh, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. \q Các ngươi đem đến những con vật bị cướp, què hay bệnh, \q rồi dâng chúng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! \q Ta có nên nhận chúng từ các ngươi không? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 또 너희는 "보라, 얼마나 수고스러운가!" 하고 말하며 그것을 코웃음 친다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희가 빼앗은 것과 다리 저는 것과 병든 것을 가져오고, \q 그 제물을 가져온다! \q 내가 그것을 너희 손에서 받겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 너희는 "이 얼마나 귀찮은 일인가!" 하며 코웃음을 친다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희가 빼앗은 짐승이나 다리 절거나 병든 짐승을 가져와서, \q 그것을 제물이라고 바친다! \q 내가 너희 손에서 그것을 받아야 하겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희는 "이 일이 이제 지긋지긋하다!" 하며 코웃음을 친다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 너희는 빼앗은 짐승이나 다리 절거나 병든 짐승을 가져와서 \q 나에게 바친다! \q 내가 그것을 너희에게서 받아야 하겠느냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: you sniff at it: you snort at it in contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to blow or puff. The priests sniff at their duty as at something worthless. |

decisions.choice: at it: at the altar and its service
decisions.reason: Jewish scribal tradition lists this among a few places where the scribes changed a word out of reverence: it says that the original read "you sniff at me" and that "at it" was written instead. The meaning is the same in the end: contempt for the service is contempt for the LORD.

decisions.choice: what was stolen: animals taken by robbery
decisions.reason: The word means taken by force. An animal gained by robbery could not be offered (Leviticus 5:23 in the Hebrew numbering). Some take it as an animal mauled by a wild beast, which also could not be offered (Exodus 22:30).

decisions.choice: animals that were stolen, or lame or sick (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "animals". The priests' words are set in double quotes. |

decisions.choice: "mnaibeua" for "sniff at it"; "walionyang'anywa" for what was taken by robbery
decisions.reason: "Kubeua" is to turn up one's nose at something in contempt, the sense of meaning decision m1; the animals were taken by force (m3), so "kunyang'anywa" rather than "kuibwa".

source.text: וְאָר֣וּר נוֹכֵ֗ל וְיֵ֤שׁ בְּעֶדְרוֹ֙ זָכָ֔ר וְנֹדֵ֛ר וְזֹבֵ֥חַ מָשְׁחָ֖ת לַֽאדֹנָ֑י כִּי֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ גָּד֜וֹל אָ֗נִי אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּשְׁמִ֖י נוֹרָ֥א בַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And cursed [is the] cheat, and [there is] in his flock a male, and [he] vows and sacrifices a blemished [one] to [the] Lord; for a great king [am] I, says Yahweh of hosts, and my name [is] feared among the nations.

en.L: Cursed is the cheat who has a male in {{gender:their|his}} flock, \q and vows [it], but sacrifices a blemished [animal] to the Lord; \q for a great King [am] I, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is feared among the nations.
en.B: Cursed is the cheat who has a sound male in {{gender:their|his}} flock and vows to give it, \q but then sacrifices to the Lord an animal with a blemish! \q I am a great King, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is feared among the nations.
en.R: A curse on anyone who cheats like this! They have a good male animal in their flock and promise to give it, \q but then they offer the Lord an animal that has something wrong with it. \q I am a great King, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q and the nations fear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

es.L: Maldito el tramposo que tiene en su rebaño un macho, \q y hace voto, pero sacrifica al Señor un [animal] dañado; \q porque yo [soy] un gran Rey, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es temido entre las naciones.
es.B: ¡Maldito el tramposo que tiene en su rebaño un macho sano y promete darlo, \q pero luego sacrifica al Señor un animal con defecto! \q Yo soy un gran Rey, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre es temido entre las naciones.
es.R: ¡Maldito sea el que hace trampa así! Tiene un buen macho en su rebaño y promete darlo, \q pero luego le ofrece al Señor un animal que tiene algún defecto. \q Yo soy un gran Rey, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q y las naciones temen {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.

fr.L: Maudit soit le tricheur qui a un mâle dans son troupeau, \q et fait un vœu, mais sacrifie au Seigneur une [bête] tarée ; \q car je suis un grand Roi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est redouté parmi les nations.
fr.B: Maudit soit le tricheur qui a dans son troupeau un mâle sans défaut et le promet par un vœu, \q puis sacrifie au Seigneur une bête qui a un défaut ! \q Je suis un grand Roi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom est redouté parmi les nations.
fr.R: Maudit soit celui qui triche ainsi ! Il a un bon mâle dans son troupeau et promet de le donner, \q mais ensuite il offre au Seigneur une bête qui a un défaut. \q Je suis un grand Roi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q et les nations craignent {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.

sw.L: Na alaaniwe mdanganyifu aliye na dume katika kundi lake, \q naye huweka nadhiri, lakini humtolea Bwana dhabihu [mnyama] mwenye kasoro; \q kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni Mfalme mkuu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q na jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} linaogopwa kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Alaaniwe mdanganyifu aliye na dume mzima katika kundi lake na kuweka nadhiri kumtoa, \q lakini kisha anamtolea Bwana dhabihu mnyama mwenye kasoro! \q Mimi ni Mfalme mkuu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q na jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} linaogopwa kati ya mataifa.
sw.R: Alaaniwe kila mtu anayedanganya hivyo! Ana dume mzuri katika kundi lake na anaahidi kumtoa, \q lakini kisha anamtolea Bwana mnyama mwenye kasoro. \q Mimi ni Mfalme mkuu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q na mataifa yanaliogopa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.

vi.L: Đáng rủa thay kẻ gian lận, là kẻ có con đực trong bầy mình, \q và hứa nguyện, nhưng lại dâng cho Chúa một [con vật] có tì vết; \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Vua lớn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đáng kính sợ giữa các dân tộc.
vi.B: Đáng rủa thay kẻ gian lận có con đực lành lặn trong bầy mình và đã hứa nguyện dâng nó, \q nhưng rồi lại dâng cho Chúa một con vật có tì vết! \q Ta là Vua lớn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được kính sợ giữa các dân tộc.
vi.R: Kẻ nào gian lận như thế sẽ bị rủa sả! Người ấy có con đực tốt trong bầy và hứa dâng nó, \q nhưng rồi lại dâng cho Chúa một con vật có tật. \q Ta là Vua vĩ đại, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán, \q và các dân tộc kính sợ danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 속이는 자는 저주를 받는다. 그의 떼 가운데 수컷이 있는데, \q 서원하고서도 흠 있는 [짐승]을 주님께 제물로 바친다. \q 나는 큰 왕이다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 내 이름은 민족들 가운데서 두려움의 대상이다.
ko.B: 자기 떼에 흠 없는 수컷이 있어서 그것을 바치겠다고 서원하고는, \q 흠 있는 짐승을 주님께 제물로 바치는 사기꾼은 저주를 받을 것이다! \q 나는 큰 왕이다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 내 이름은 민족들 가운데서 두려움을 받는다.
ko.R: 이렇게 속이는 사람은 누구든지 저주를 받을 것이다! 그는 떼 가운데 좋은 수컷이 있어서 그것을 바치겠다고 약속하고는, \q 정작 주님께는 어딘가 탈이 난 짐승을 바친다. \q 나는 위대한 왕이다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 민족들이 내 이름을 두려워한다.

decisions.choice: a male, a vow, a blemished animal: a vow paid with a defective animal
decisions.reason: A vow offering had to be a male without defect (Leviticus 22:18-21). The cheat has a good animal but brings a damaged one, keeping the better for himself. |

decisions.choice: I am a great King: the LORD is King over all nations
decisions.reason: "Great king" was a title of the emperors of Assyria and Persia (2 Kings 18:19). The LORD is the great King over all the earth (Psalm 47:3; 95:3), whose name the nations fear (verse 11). He deserves better than the governor of verse 8. |

decisions.choice: feared: held in awe
decisions.reason: The word means "to be feared", awesome, as in Zephaniah 2:11. |

decisions.choice: the Lord (Adonai); King with a capital K; the gender setting for the cheat
decisions.reason: "Lord" stands for Adonai, as the settled wording for this title of God. "King" is capitalized as a title of God. The cheat may be any owner of a flock, so Literal and Balanced use the gender setting and Readable says "anyone ... they". |

decisions.choice: no gender span: "su rebaño"
decisions.reason: The English uses the gender setting for the cheat's "their / his" flock; Spanish "su" already covers both, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "son troupeau"
decisions.reason: French "son" agrees with the flock, not the owner, so it already covers both; the English gender span has no French counterpart.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "kundi lake"
decisions.reason: Swahili "-ake" covers both sexes, so the English gender span needs no counterpart.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "bầy mình"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "mình" covers both sexes, so the English gender span needs no counterpart.

decisions.choice: no gender span: 그의 떼 / 자기 떼
decisions.reason: Korean 자기 and 그 here carry no gender contrast that a setting could change, so the English span needs no counterpart.
